newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudi barley deal seen taking shape overnight.
newsitem.headline: Saudi barley deal seen taking shape overnight.

text.p: Grain traders said on Wednesday Saudi Arabia's latest barley purchase was expected to take shape overnight amid signs that prices could be lower than some had expected.
Saudi Arabia invited bids on Tuesday to supply one million tonnes of the grain in September and October.

Traders said prices offered appeared to suggest lowest offers were worth close to $120 per tonne fob. One senior trader said offers on a delivered basis with freight were seen in a wide range starting from $142 per tonne. Highest offers could as much as $158 per tonne, he said, while others pegged highest realistic offers at $150.

The tender sparked intense competition despite the fairly tight supply/demand balance predicted for barley with demand outstripping output by two percent this year. Traders said they did not expect final word on the purchase until at least Thursday morning.
"We won't know for 24 hours. I think it's happening tonight," one European trader said.
Traders were uncertain whether Canada's reluctance to join in by offering more than one barley cargo signalled real concern about supplies or merely a bullish price outlook.
A cash grain source said in Canada on Tuesday that the Canadian Wheat Board had allocated just one cargo for current business, saying farmers were not delivering.
Equally uncertain was the European Union's export policy after EU agriculture director Guy Legras on Tuesday reiterated Brussels was in no hurry to open stalled subsidy tenders.

Analysts said Legras' statement at EU farm talks in Luxembourg was a usual bid to dampen export speculation but it was unlikely he would give anything away while ministers were still negotiating a crucial price accord.

Fob world barley prices for the northern hemisphere recently been pegged at or near $130 per tonne, traders said. Freight, colouring and other costs for barley shipped to Saudi Arabia amount to $20-22 per tonne, traders said.
A small proportion of barley imported to Saudi Arabia must be dyed to distinguish it from local crop.
There were unconfirmed reports Iran bought 50,000 tonnes of barley at $127-128 per tonne for October shipment.
